mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% in a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the signal, or the correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% in a month indicates a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate reduced consumer spending and economic slowdown.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5d returns in > 70% of triggered instances despite the signal, or the correlation between UNRATE increases and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A significant decline in real GDP growth by more than 1% quarter-over-quarter signals a weakening demand environment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as businesses and consumers cut back on spending.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the signal, or the correlation between GDPC1 declines and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production by more than 2% month-over-month signals a strong supply-side response, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as increased production capacity supports economic growth.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the signal, or the correlation between INDPRO increases and positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained period of low inflation (CPIAUCSL growth < 2% YoY) coupled with low unemployment (UNRATE < 5%) signals a stable economic environment, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as businesses and consumers benefit from predictable economic conditions.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the signal, or the joint condition of low inflation and low unemployment does not correlate with positive SPX returns (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 10% month-over-month signals a strong demand for housing, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as increased construction activity boosts economic growth.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the signal, or the correlation between HOUST increases and positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 200,000 jobs per month for two consecutive months signals a strong labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as increased employment supports consumer spending and economic growth.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases > 200k jobs for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in > 70% of triggered instances despite the signal, or the correlation between PAYEMS increases and positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in retail and food services sales (RSAFS) by more than 5% month-over-month signals a strong consumer demand, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as increased consumer spending supports economic growth.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 60% of instances despite the signal, or the correlation between RSAFS increases and positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
